title: OpenSearch red status runbook
brief: Quarry Press runs a nine-node OpenSearch cluster called search-prod behind the article search and the subscriber archive. Can you write the on-call runbook for when the cluster goes red? Start with "Symptoms": the CLUSTER_RED alert fires, search returns partial or empty results, and the editors report that new articles do not appear. Then "Triage": check cluster health with GET _cluster/health and note the number of unassigned shards, then ask the cluster why with GET _cluster/allocation/explain. The usual causes are disk watermarks (low 85 percent, high 90 percent, flood stage 95 percent), a lost data node, or a bad index template after a deploy. Then "Fix by cause" with steps in order, each with sub-steps. 1 Disk watermark: a) find the fullest nodes with GET _cat/allocation?v, b) delete indices older than 90 from the logs-* family, but never touch articles-* or archive-*, c) once disk is under 80 percent clear the read-only block with PUT _all/_settings setting index.blocks.read_only_allow_delete to null, d) wait for the shards to relocate. 2 Lost data node: a) check the instance in the AWS console, b) if it is gone, let the autoscaling group replace it, usually 6 to 8 minutes, c) shard recovery then takes about 20 minutes for the 1.2 TB per node. 3 Bad index template: a) find the last deploy in #deploys, b) roll the template back using the saved copy in the search-config repository, c) reindex the affected index. Readers must be told firmly before any deletion: never delete an index without a snapshot taken in the last 24 hours, because the archive cannot be rebuilt. Finish with "Escalation": page the Search Infrastructure lead if the cluster is still red after 30 minutes, and open an incident in #incidents.

edit.request: Change the cleanup retention from 90 days to 60 days, and add a new step under Lost data node: "Confirm the replacement node has joined with GET _cat/nodes".
